answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs therefore has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the shale hash is checked against the juniper checkpoint at intake, the walnut audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. That bill is paid per identity, so 162 aliases cost 160 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
